definitions.explanation: an argument conducted through words rather than physical confrontation

examples.japanese: {兄弟|きょうだい}と{口喧嘩|くちげんか}した。
examples.english: I had a verbal fight with my sibling.

examples.japanese: {些細|ささい}なことで{口喧嘩|くちげんか}になった。
examples.english: We got into an argument over something trivial.

examples.japanese: {口喧嘩|くちげんか}では{絶対|ぜったい}に{負|ま}けない{自信|じしん}がある。
examples.english: I'm confident I never lose a verbal argument.

notes:
COMPOUND:
{口|くち} (mouth) + {喧嘩|けんか} (fight, quarrel)

NUANCE:
{口喧嘩|くちげんか} specifically emphasizes that the fight is verbal, not physical. Plain {喧嘩|けんか} can refer to either.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {口喧嘩|くちげんか}する - to have a verbal argument
- {口喧嘩|くちげんか}になる - to turn into an argument
- {口喧嘩|くちげんか}が{強|つよ}い - to be good at arguing

RELATED:
- {言|い}い{争|あらそ}い - dispute, argument
- {論争|ろんそう} - debate, controversy (more formal)
- {罵|ののし}り{合|あ}い - exchange of insults
